title: The Mystery of Sharp Edges and Wide Tracks
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about everyday applications of pressure.

questions.prompt: What happens to pressure when the same force acts over a smaller area?
choices: Pressure decreases
Pressure increases
Pressure stays the same
Pressure becomes zero
questions.explanation: For the same force, a smaller contact area produces greater pressure (P = F / A).

questions.prompt: Which situation produces less pressure on the ground?
choices: A tractor with narrow tyres
A person standing on one foot
A snow vehicle with continuous tracks
A sharp knife cutting an apple
questions.explanation: Continuous tracks spread the force over a larger contact area, so pressure on the ground is less.

questions.prompt: A boy weighs 400 N. If he stands on one foot with a contact area of 0.01 m², what pressure does he exert?
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force ÷ Area = 400 N ÷ 0.01 m² = 40,000 Pa.

questions.prompt: If a boy changes from standing on both feet to standing on one foot, what happens to his pressure on the ground?
choices: It decreases because his weight decreases
It increases because the contact area becomes smaller
It stays the same because his mass is unchanged
It becomes zero because one foot is lifted
questions.explanation: His weight stays the same, but standing on one foot halves the contact area, so pressure increases.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains the relationship between force, area, and pressure?
choices: For the same force, a larger contact area produces greater pressure
For the same force, a smaller contact area produces greater pressure
Pressure does not depend on contact area
Pressure always increases when weight stays the same
questions.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by area, so the same force over a smaller area means greater pressure.
